Get yourself out there. You say you're 19/m, you probably have a bit of free time. I volunteered and it made me meet all kinds of people, from people younger than me, same age as me and people ages 65+, and all different kinds of people, each with vastly different outlooks on life.

You'll not be so lonely when you are interacting with such a broad range of people. Personally I volunteered at a charity shop, and I loved every second of it, I stayed there for 3 years before I moved house and had to stop. When I first signed up there it was actually just to get something on my CV/Resume, I thought it would suck, and then I quickly realised how much I enjoyed the company. I got a weekday job and still did voluntary work on my weekends because I liked it so much.

You could also volunteer at animal shelters, hospices, soup kitchens, churches, social clubs, whatever tickles your fancy. A similar thing would be work experience. You only need to do 4-8 hours a week of this and it really does lift your mood.

You could also take up a hobby, woodworking classes, cooking classes and gaming clubs are great places to meet people. (And they won't be the type of sex/drug obsessed people you find out at clubs)

Visit family, maybe go fishing with your grand dad or go for tea and cake with your grandma. I'm sure they'd be happy for the company.

There are a bunch of things you could do to deal with the loneliness you're feeling. Good luck and feel free to talk to me any time you feel isolated or need advice. I used to suffer from loneliness too and I know it can get tough.
